obligations.note: At head, all three INTEGRATIONS base_urls are still https. The new branch in url_for calls base.replace("https://", "https://", 1), which leaves the URL unchanged, so every outbound endpoint, including statement-delivery /archive/ paths, stays https. This rests on reading the code; the CI control-test result is not relied on (see CHG-4).

The INTEGRATIONS list (core-banking, sanctions-screening, statement-delivery) and its hosts are unchanged. All three are listed in controls/payments/asset-inventory.json with an owner and a data classification.
Ticket CHG-25162 (standard) was approved by change manager Grace Kim at 2026-10-22T23:23Z, before review. Its components include payments.integrations, the only component the change touches.
Mara Costa approved code_review on the head commit. She holds change_approver for payments and is not the author, Aisha Bello.
The change has a single commit, ef417ae8, and every approval names it, so no later commits could void them.

run.json says ci-runner-01 ran commit ef417ae8 starting 2026-10-23T11:23Z. The attached JUnit report was instead generated on hostname dev-laptop-7.local at 2026-10-23T20:50Z, a developer workstation of someone not in the directory, at a time unrelated to the run. The report therefore is not valid CI evidence that the suite and the ENC-2/INV-1 control tests passed on the final commit.
integrations.py belongs to payments.integrations, which is security_sensitive. Kofi Mensah, a security_reviewer, approved security_review on the head commit.
The ledger entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, Approvals.java, Underwriting.java and Policy.java. None of these are touched by this change, so no accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The code change is functionally a no-op: replacing https:// with https:// changes nothing, so endpoints stay on TLS and the integration inventory is unchanged. The ticket, independent code review and security review are all valid and cover the head commit. However, the CI test report attached to the run was produced on a personal workstation at a time inconsistent with the recorded CI run, so it is not valid evidence that the suite passed on the final commit. CHG-4 is refuted, and the change is rejected until a genuine CI run on the head commit is supplied.
